correctness.rationale: Nonadjacent pairs are exactly same-part pairs. For distinct vertices in one part, every third vertex has equal distance to the pair, so the only distinguishers are the two endpoints. Thus nonlocal resolution is equivalent to omitting at most one vertex from each non-singleton part. Independent partwise counting proves the minimum, enumerator, and basis count. The direct verifier confirms all statements for every connected complete multipartite isomorphism type through order ten.

value.rationale: The theorem is a natural complete classification on a standard graph family. It determines every nonlocal resolving set, the full size distribution, the minimum, and every minimum basis in one factored law. This extends the defining paper's complete-bipartite endpoint to arbitrary multipartite profiles and supplies exact benchmark data for the newer nonlocal metric-dimension theory.
